title: A dental pain pathway to reduce antibiotic prescribing in general practice: protocol for a cluster randomised trial
abstract: Objective: to test whether a dental pain pathway reduces antibiotic prescribing for dental pain in general practice without increasing emergency attendance for dental infection. Design: two-arm cluster randomised trial in 11 practices over 12 months. Primary outcome: antibiotic prescription within 3 days of a dental pain consultation. Results will follow the trial.
introduction: Antibiotics do not relieve most dental pain, but GPs prescribe them when patients cannot reach dental care. A pathway supplying same-day dental advice may change this.
methods: Practices allocated in strata by size and deprivation; routine coded outcomes; mixed-effects analysis; independent safety review.
results: No data have been collected yet.
discussion: The discussion will compare the results with the retrieved trial and consider generalisability to districts with poor dental access.
limitations: Few clusters; reliance on coding; one district.
conclusion: To be written after the trial.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for cluster randomised trials; SPIRIT for the protocol
summary: Trial protocol structure with results left empty.
